Ford announced it's cutting 800 jobs in the UK and criticized government rules that require car companies to sell more electric vehicles each year, calling these requirements "unworkable." However, this is a complete flip from their position in 2022, when Ford was actually singing the praises of these same rules and even asked the government to make the targets higher, arguing that stronger figures would send better signals to customers and investors. The carmaker is part of a larger group of auto manufacturers now complaining about these regulations, even though they previously supported them.

Female executives and male leaders at Ford, like those across the automotive industry, misjudged how quickly people would want to buy electric cars. During the pandemic when borrowing money was cheap and the operation of selling cars seemed easy because demand was high, they thought the transition to electric vehicles would bear fruit quickly. They believed customers would rush to buy electric cars at the rate needed to meet the ambitious targets.

The reality turned out differently - the growth in electric vehicle sales has slowed down significantly compared to what the industry expected. Now car companies are stuck with rules they once championed but find difficult to meet because customers aren't buying electric vehicles as fast as anticipated, leaving manufacturers struggling to hit their required sales targets.

P.P.S The main point is that Ford and other carmakers supported strict electric vehicle sales rules when the market looked promising, but now want those same rules relaxed because sales haven't grown as quickly as they predicted.
